title: Vectorial bent functions above the half-dimension threshold outside planar projections
summary: Determine whether a vectorial bent function with output dimension strictly above half its input dimension can lie outside all planar-function projections.

formal_statement.body: Does there exist a prime $p$, dimensions $n$ and $m$ with $m>\lceil n/2\rceil$, and a vectorial bent function $F:V_n^{(p)}\to V_m^{(p)}$ that is not a projection of any planar function? Equivalently, either exhibit and prove one such nonprojection witness or prove that every vectorial bent function in this dimension range is a planar-function projection.

scope.domain: Vectorial bent functions between finite-dimensional vector spaces over prime fields
assumptions: $V_n^{(p)}$ and $V_m^{(p)}$ are vector spaces over $\mathbb F_p$
$F$ is vectorial bent in the source's nonzero-component sense
Nonprojection means that $F$ is not representable as a projection of any planar function
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later public result exhibits a vectorial bent function satisfying both the strict dimension inequality and the planar-nonprojection condition, or proves the universal opposite statement. An inaccessible construction paper has no compatible public resolution signal outside its title.

citations.label: Cesmelioglu--Meidl, high-output vectorial bent nonprojection question

progress.summary: The TIT source asks whether the known planar and projected-planar examples exhaust vectorial bent functions above the half-dimension threshold.
